claims.text: The onset and progression of phase transition in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by stochastic principles of particle formation.
Inhibition of precursor mobility during particle formation favors formation of a single phase.
The particles under study are initially solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Exposure to the premelting and melting regime is the intervention intended to induce the transition.
Nanoparticle size and shape are relevant conditions governing the thermal phase-transition behavior.
Limited precursor mobility is the structural mediator controlling the response of the initially solid particles during premelting and melting.
A stochastic formation mechanism with inhibited precursor mobility produces a single-phase alloy.
Heating in the specified regime will produce a single-phase FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle.
The resulting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle will have uniform composition and structure.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have non-uniform composition and structure.
The applicable mechanism is bounded by the premelting/melting temperature range and by nanoparticle size and shape.
The exact temperature range, size, and shape that favor single-phase formation are unknown.
Combined in situ X-ray powder diffraction and multi-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy can probe nanoparticle formation mechanisms.
Absence of a single-phase FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle under the predicted conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The material is specified as already-formed, initially solid nanoparticles undergoing premelting and melting, but the proposed mediator and mechanism concern inhibited precursor mobility during initial particle formation. No dissolution, atomization, or reformation step is specified that would make precursor mobility operative during heating of existing particles.
